author: original (NevaIB)
title: Introduction to integration

points.text: Using a boundary condition to find the constant
Area between a curve and the x-axis when the curve is above the axis

bigPicture: Integration reverses differentiation, and a definite integral gives the area under a curve. This first pass covers polynomials and GDC integrals.

keyIdeas.answer: ∫ax^n dx = a x^(n+1)/(n + 1) + C, n ≠ −1. Rewrite roots and reciprocals as powers first.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find the constant C?
keyIdeas.answer: Substitute a known point (boundary condition) into F(x) + C and solve for C.
∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx on the GDC; write the integral with its limits in your working before the answer.

keyIdeas.cue: Area between a curve and the x-axis when the curve is above it?
keyIdeas.answer: Area = ∫ₐᵇ y dx, provided y ≥ 0 between a and b.

keyTerms.def: a function whose derivative is f
C, fixed by a boundary condition

misconceptions.right: n = −1 is the exception (it gives ln x, in 5.10).

practice.prompt: Find the area enclosed by y = 4 + 3x − x², the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 4.
commonErrors: Not checking the curve is above the axis

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

given.item: ∫x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n + 1) + C, n ≠ −1; area between y = f(x) and the x-axis, f(x) > 0: A = ∫ₐᵇ y dx

memorise: Rewrite roots and fractions as powers
